title: Statement of Purpose
intro: A short reflection on where I am heading, what I chose to put in this portfolio, and why those pieces matter.

sections.heading: My goals
sections.summary: Short-term and long-term, professional and academic.
sections.body:
In the short term, I would like to find a marketing internship for next summer, ideally one where I can work on brand or campaign strategy directly rather than just supporting it. I have some experience with running promotion and event marketing for my badminton club at my former high school. In the long term, I hope to work in brand and campaign strategy for companies in the tech industry, since science and technology are two things I'm genuinely passionate about. I'm currently studying Business Administration with a concentration in Marketing at VinUniversity, on a merit scholarship.

This class is practical enough to translate directly into making a CV, writing a cover letter, and building a professional LinkedIn page — the first "real life" tools I can use to get in front of people who might actually hire me.

sections.heading: Why these documents
sections.summary: The package I chose and what each piece is doing here.
sections.body:
I chose the Job Seeking package over the Study Exchange package because I'm not applying anywhere — I'm trying to get a job. These three documents are what an employer sees before contacting me about a role.

My CV changed the most. Initially, I had included a personal profile (including photo and date of birth) followed by a list of my academic achievements. That's suitable for a university application, but not for job seeking, since it says nothing about the work I'm actually capable of doing. I restructured the CV to lead with Education, then Leadership & Activities, and Awards last. I also consolidated fifteen individual awards into five grouped lines so they don't dominate the page.

I wrote the Marketing Specialist cover letter in concrete terms rather than generic ones. My LinkedIn profile is the version of me that shows up first when someone searches my name, so it has to hold up without me there to explain it.

sections.heading: How I've grown as a writer
sections.summary: What changed in how I write, and what still needs work.
sections.body:
Initially I saw the CV and the portfolio as two lists of all my work ever. However, through this assignment, I've realized the CV is meant to grab an employer's attention in the first ten seconds. The portfolio is meant to prove the claims I make in my CV. So my CV and this portfolio site ended up built for different audiences and purposes.

The best feedback I got in my third peer review was on my CV's accomplishments section. First, I only wrote out what I did — not what it produced. So I went back through every bullet on my CV. Finding real numbers for some of them was harder than I expected, so I either added numbers to support the claim or cut the line entirely. I'm not sure every claim on my CV can be fully quantified, but that's the honest gap I'm bringing into whatever I write next.
